hypotheses.claim: Intent interface, canonical semantic IR, model-native symbolic deliberation and physical neural/runtime representation are causally distinct layers; bundled AI-native comparisons misattribute effects.
hypotheses.counter: One monolithic AI-native treatment is sufficient because the layers only matter jointly.
hypotheses.falsifier: Orthogonal layer interventions show no separable effects or interactions and a single bundled treatment predicts held-out outcomes equally well.

hypotheses.claim: Compiling ambiguous natural-language intent into typed Clay goals, hard constraints, soft preferences and explicit unknowns reduces silent intent drift versus direct vibe-to-action generation.
hypotheses.counter: A sufficiently adapted Clay-native model can preserve intent without an explicit L0->L1 compiler.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target/twin tasks show no reliability, reproducibility or authority benefit after matching model/context and compiler cost.
hypotheses.experiment: L0 raw intent vs typed intent-contract factorial

hypotheses.claim: Canonical Clay/ClayCode IR plus deterministic execution provides an independent benefit even when the model is not Clay-native, analogous to AINL's compile-once/run-many architecture.
hypotheses.counter: All gains attributed to canonical IR disappear after controlling for prompt compactness and model quality.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched semantic/token/runtime benchmark shows no correctness, repeatability, cost or authority advantage.
hypotheses.experiment: prompt-loop vs canonical Clay plan vs compiled COVE plan repeated-run benchmark

hypotheses.claim: Full-model Clay-native adaptation yields an L2 benefit beyond deterministic L1 compilation by reducing reconstruction burden and improving unseen Clay composition.
hypotheses.counter: A strong general model consuming compiled Clay performs as well as a fully adapted Clay-native model.
hypotheses.falsifier: Pinned target Qwen factorial finds no main effect or useful interaction for full-model Clay adaptation after L1/view controls.
hypotheses.experiment: target Qwen general-vs-full-FT Clay x raw-vs-compiled Clay view

hypotheses.claim: A learned discrete VQ/codebook bottleneck may improve interpretability/communication in a Clay-native model but is not required by the fixed Clay-native architecture and may trade off accuracy/generalization.
hypotheses.counter: Discrete bottleneck is necessary for genuine AI mother-tongue behavior and uniformly improves reasoning.
hypotheses.falsifier: Clay-native model without VQ matches/exceeds VQ arm on causal interpretability, compositional/OOD performance and efficiency, or VQ degrades retained capability.
hypotheses.experiment: Clay-native full-FT ± discrete codebook auxiliary pathway

hypotheses.claim: Symbol purity or recurrence is not evidence of causal symbolic reasoning; usefulness requires permutation/lesion, mechanistic rescue, OOD and hidden-state mediation tests.
hypotheses.counter: High-purity stable symbols are sufficient evidence that the symbols implement reasoning.
hypotheses.falsifier: Purity alone prospectively predicts causal necessity across held-out tasks without intervention evidence.

hypotheses.claim: CLAY_CANONICAL and CLAY_MODEL should share semantic identities while allowing different density/local handles/serialization; forcing identical textual forms wastes context and increases coupling.
hypotheses.counter: One literal serialization across canonical store and model view maximizes semantic unity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Identical-form design Pareto-dominates compiled model views on correctness, context, latency and recovery while preserving exact semantics.
hypotheses.experiment: canonical verbose vs compiled model dialect with roundtrip/property checks

hypotheses.claim: Semantic unification reduces translation mismatch but increases common-mode semantic/compiler risk, so H4 typed firebreaks become more important as Clay fluency rises.
hypotheses.counter: Native-language fluency makes semantic firebreaks redundant.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adaptive fault injection shows no increase in correlated blast radius and firebreaks provide no safety/recovery benefit in a Clay-native target.
hypotheses.experiment: common-mode compiler/ontology fault x typed-firebreak factorial

hypotheses.claim: A vibe/preference is a soft optimization target and must not acquire FACT_EXACT, AUTHORITY_CAP or EFFECT_INTENT semantics without explicit trusted casts.
hypotheses.counter: Model interpretation can safely infer when a vibe implies authority/correctness constraints.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial intent tasks show implicit authority inference is equally safe and more useful under irreversible effects.
hypotheses.experiment: typed preference vs implicit vibe authority attack

hypotheses.claim: GWT experiments in C6 must add language/view state as orthogonal factors; improved output after Clay training can otherwise be caused by projection or canonical-IR changes rather than workspace dynamics.
hypotheses.counter: Once model and workspace both speak Clay, projection/language factors disappear as causal confounds.
hypotheses.falsifier: Pinned-semantic tests show language/view interventions never change uptake/output independently of workspace selection.
hypotheses.experiment: L1 view x L2 native-language x workspace selection x re-entry factorial

hypotheses.claim: ClayGraph + a Clay-native model can reduce memory/cognition impedance, but pre-activated association must be tested against truthful/shuffled/no-field controls and cannot be inferred from same-language recurrence.
hypotheses.counter: Shared Clay semantics alone guarantees useful memory integration.
hypotheses.falsifier: Truthful field fails to outperform matched shuffled/no-field controls or increases false-support propagation.
hypotheses.experiment: target model truthful vs relation-shuffled vs temporal-shuffled vs no latent field

hypotheses.claim: AINL-style compile-once/run-many savings and C6 native-language benefits are orthogonal: stable deterministic routines should avoid repeated model reasoning even with a Clay-native model.
hypotheses.counter: A native Clay model is cheap/reliable enough that deterministic compilation offers no recurring advantage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated-run benchmark finds model-loop path equal/better on correctness, token/energy/latency and recovery after compile amortization.
hypotheses.experiment: repeated operation economics with state-change sensitivity

hypotheses.claim: Tokenizer compatibility is a separate L2 implementation variable; preserving old token IDs while adding a small set of high-value Clay primitives/local handles may outperform unchanged tokenization without requiring a new latent language.
hypotheses.counter: Full-model adaptation eliminates tokenizer fertility as an important constraint.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target checkpoints show no efficiency/learning/generalization benefit from Clay-aware tokenization under matched training compute.
hypotheses.experiment: unchanged BBPE vs appended Clay primitives vs continued Clay merge learning
